regolith_bulk_density_kgm3.note: Measured in situ: InSight HP3 mole thermal sensors give 1211 (+149/-113) kg/m^3 for the top ~40 cm (Grott et al. 2021, JGR Planets 126, e2021JE006861). Viking landers (Moore et al. 1987, USGS PP 1389): drift ~1150-1200, crusty-to-cloddy ~1400, blocky ~1600 kg/m^3. MGS-1 (Rocknest/Curiosity-based simulant) bulk ~1160 kg/m^3. +/-25% (908-1514) spans drift through crusty-cloddy soils; excludes blocky (1600) and grain density (~2580-2900).

extrusion_rate_kg_per_h.note: Derived from ICON Vulcan II published spec: 1 in tall x 2 in wide bead at 5-7 in/s (mid 6 in/s) = 12 in^3/s = 0.708 m^3/h; x 2300 kg/m^3 (Portland-cement 'Lavacrete' mortar, typical printable mortar 2100-2300) = 1628 kg/h. 5 in/s -> 1357 kg/h, 7 in/s -> 1900 kg/h; 25% band (1221-2035) covers the published speed range plus mortar density uncertainty. This is peak nozzle throughput, not a duty-cycle-averaged rate.

energy_per_kg_kWh.note: Printer electrical energy per kg extruded = 16 kW nominal / 1628 kg/h = 0.0098 kWh/kg. Range 0.0084 (16 kW, 7 in/s) to 0.026 (35 kW peak, 5 in/s). Excludes embodied energy of cement/binder and any sintering. 50% band (0.0049-0.0147) because only nominal/peak power and a speed range are published.

printer_power_kW.note: ICON Vulcan II: nominal consumption 16 kW, up to 35 kW peak (ICON statement reported by Fabbaloo/3Dnatives/VoxelMatters). Value is nominal; 25% band (12-20 kW). A sim using peak 35 kW would fail by design.

landing_pad_10m_diam_20cm_mass_t.note: Derived: V = pi x 5^2 x 0.20 = 15.708 m^3; x 1211 kg/m^3 (InSight measured bulk density) = 19.02 t. Tolerance inherits the density band (+/-25%: 14.3-23.8 t). NOTE: if the sim uses sintered/consolidated material density (~2000-2500 kg/m^3) the pad is 31-39 t and falls outside; the spec asks to derive from regolith bulk density.

landing_pad_print_time_h.note: Derived two ways with the Vulcan II rate: mass-based 19.02 t / 1628 kg/h = 11.7 h; volume-based 15.708 m^3 / 0.708 m^3/h = 22.2 h (what a volumetric extruder actually limits). Value is the midpoint; 35% band (11.05-22.95 h) brackets both conventions. Continuous printing, no duty-cycle losses. For contrast, ESA PAVER laser-melting estimate is 115 days for a 100 m^2 x 2 cm lunar pad (different, much slower process).

sintering_energy_per_kg_kWh.note: Sources disagree by two orders of magnitude, so loose. Central value derived from ESA PAVER (Gines-Palomares et al. 2023, Sci. Rep. 13:15593): 12 kW CO2 laser, 100 m^2 x 2 cm pad in 115 days -> 33.1 MWh / (2 m^3 x 2000-2500 kg/m^3) = 6.6-8.3 kWh/kg. Lower bound physics: Whittington & Parsapoor 2022 heat-to-1000 C enthalpy ~810 J/g = 0.225 kWh/kg (sintering), 1775 J/g = 0.49 kWh/kg (full melt) - 100%-efficiency floor. Upper: domestic-microwave sintering of lunar simulant measured 69-98 MJ/kg = 19-27 kWh/kg (2024 J. Eur. Ceram. Soc. S0955221924009208, bench scale). 70% band (2.1-11.9) = realistic process energy with losses; excludes ideal-thermodynamic and bench-microwave extremes.

polymer_part_rate_g_per_h.note: Commercial FDM (Bambu Lab X1-Carbon): official max hotend flow 32 mm^3/s (143 g/h PLA at 1.24 g/cm^3); default Bambu PLA profile volumetric limit 12 mm^3/s -> 54 g/h; users report 18-21 mm^3/s sustainable (80-94 g/h). Real parts average below the limit (travel, perimeters, cooling). 60% band (21.6-86.4 g/h) covers practical sustained rates; the 143 g/h hardware ceiling is excluded as unrealistic for whole parts.
